title: Cloud SLA service ticket resolution time percentile
scenario_markdown: Resolution time $X$ (in hours) for cloud infrastructure support tickets follows an exponential distribution with rate parameter $\lambda = 0.40$ tickets resolved per hour (mean resolution time $\mu = 1/\lambda = 2.5$ hours). Management wishes to establish a 90th percentile Service Level Agreement (SLA) target $x^*$, such that $90\%$ of tickets are resolved within $x^*$ hours ($P(X \le x^*) = 0.90$).
assumptions: Continuous exponential resolution time X ~ Exp(lambda = 0.40)

approval.notes: Verified quantile derivation: 1 - exp(-0.40 * x*) = 0.90 => exp(-0.40 * x*) = 0.10 => x* = -ln(0.10)/0.40 = 2.302585/0.40 = 5.75646 hours. Rounded to two decimals is 5.76 hours. Excel formula: =-LN(1 - 0.90)/0.40.

stages.prompt_markdown: To find the 90th percentile $x^*$ where $P(X \le x^*) = 0.90$ for an exponential distribution with rate $\lambda = 0.40$, which mathematical formula isolates $x^*$?

options.hint_markdown: Linear scaling applies only to the uniform distribution $U(0, b)$; the exponential distribution is non-linear and right-skewed.
The standard normal quantile $z = 1.282$ applies only to bell-shaped normal distributions, not exponential distributions.

stages.explanation_markdown: Setting $F(x^*) = 1 - e^{-\lambda x^*} = p$ yields $e^{-\lambda x^*} = 1 - p$. Taking natural logarithms: $-\lambda x^* = \ln(1 - p) \implies x^* = -\frac{\ln(1 - p)}{\lambda} = -\frac{\ln(0.10)}{0.40}$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Evaluating $x^* = -\frac{\ln(0.10)}{0.40}$, what is the numerical 90th percentile resolution time?

options.hint_markdown: The exponential distribution is right-skewed; linear scaling applies only to uniform distributions.
Solving $1 - e^{-\lambda x^*} = 0.90$ gives $e^{-\lambda x^*} = 0.10$, so you must take $\ln(0.10)$, not $\ln(0.90)$.
The exponential distribution is not bell-shaped; using standard normal $z = 1.282$ is an approximation that ignores the exponential functional form.

stages.explanation_markdown: $x^* = -\frac{-2.302585}{0.40} \approx 5.7565$ hours (or approximately $5.76$ hours). In Excel, this quantile is computed using `=-LN(1 - 0.90)/0.40`.

stages.prompt_markdown: Notice that the 90th percentile ($5.76$ hours) is more than double the mean resolution time ($2.50$ hours). What property of the exponential distribution causes this disparity?

options.text_markdown: The exponential distribution is heavily right-skewed with a long right tail, so upper percentiles stretch far above the mean to capture infrequent high-duration cases
The disparity is a calculation anomaly; in all continuous distributions the 90th percentile is exactly $1.96$ standard deviations above the mean
options.hint_markdown: Only the normal distribution follows empirical rule standard deviation multiples. Exponential skewness causes upper percentiles to extend much further.

options.text_markdown: Analysts should instead use `=EXPON.INV(0.90, 0.40)` to enforce symmetry around the mean
options.hint_markdown: Excel does not have an `=EXPON.INV` function; quantiles must be solved algebraically using `=-LN(1-p)/lambda`.

stages.explanation_markdown: Because the exponential distribution has density $f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}$ peaking at $x = 0$ and tapering off gradually to $+\infty$, the median is $\frac{\ln(2)}{\lambda} \approx 0.693\mu$, well below the mean $\mu$. Consequently, the 90th percentile $-\frac{\ln(0.10)}{\lambda} \approx 2.303\mu$ sits far above the mean.
